summary: Wenatchee NF lookout on Little Bald Mountain, Yakima Co.: a 1936 timber tower with L-4 cab, burned in 1980. Concrete footings remain; the summit is reachable by road.

facts.design: 20-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Burned to the ground in 1980; concrete footings remain and are used as guy-line anchors

staffing.status: not replaced; Forest Service staffed Cleman Lookout instead

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Wenatchee National Forest

access.note: Drive to the summit (last two miles rough rock, per WillhiteWeb); WTA describes a trail to the summit open to hikers, cyclists, equestrians and motorcycles

visit.trail_note: WTA describes a trail that continues 4.5 miles and 1,506 feet of gain to the summit

events.note: FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb all give 1936; WillhiteWeb reads 1934 panoramas as possibly showing an earlier structure
One of the female lookouts in summer 1943 was a grade school teacher (WillhiteWeb)
Tom Bigley filled in late in summer 1958 for the regular lookout
Barbara Jones manned the lookout in the early 1970s
USGS-attributed description of a Forest Service survey disk stamped 1938 in the northeast concrete footing (as posted on the weebly page)
Cab burned to the ground during the lookout's day off; WillhiteWeb's Tom Bigley suspects a propane stove

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb date the tower to 1936. WillhiteWeb also reads 1934 panoramas as showing an earlier structure, so the story keeps 1936 and says an earlier lookout may have stood there.

sources.title: Little Bald Mountain Lookout Site - Naches Ranger District

notes_for_editor: Build year (1936) and 1980 fire agree across four sources. Today's condition rests on WillhiteWeb's photo captions (its visit photos are captioned 2016) and the WTA trail page; neither is a current status report. Staffing lines come from WillhiteWeb's reading of newspapers and blogs, and the 1943 newspaper text is reprinted on the weebly page rather than read from the original. The 1971 survey-disk description is secondhand. The FFLOS brief record (status gone, access unknown) is confirmed; access is set to public from the WillhiteWeb and WTA descriptions. No photos added.
